title: Plans & the future
goal: Talk about plans, intentions and hopes: what you will do, want to do and are planning to do.
intro:
Kannada doesn't need a separate future tense: the present-future you learned in unit 10 already means 'will' (ನಾಳೆ ಬರ್ತೀನಿ 'I'll come tomorrow'). What this unit adds is the subtle and very common ways of talking about **intentions**: 'I want to', 'I'm thinking of', 'the plan is to'.

One key contrast: ನಾನು ಹೋಗಬೇಕು 'I **have to** go' vs ನನಗೆ ಹೋಗಬೇಕು 'I **want to** go'. The only difference is the case of the subject.

vocab.note: ಬರುವ ವಾರ 'next week'; spoken ಬರೋ barō.
ನನಗೆ ... ಆಸೆ ಇದೆ 'I wish / I'd love to ...'.

vocab.en: to join; to reach; to belong

vocab.note: Stay at a hotel: ಹೋಟೆಲ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಉಳಿ / ಇರು.

vocab.en: to save (money, time); to keep back
from now on; in (time from now)
vocab.note: ಇನ್ನು ಎರಡು ದಿನದಲ್ಲಿ 'in two days' time'. Don't confuse with ಇನ್ನೂ 'still, yet'.

phrases.en: What's the plan for the weekend?
Next month I'm going to my hometown.
I'm thinking of buying a car.
I'll be there in five minutes.
I don't feel like going out today.
What are the preparations for the festival?

grammar.title: Talking about the future
grammar.body:
Use the **present-future** tense: ನಾಳೆ ಮಳೆ ಬರುತ್ತೆ 'it will rain tomorrow', ಮುಂದಿನ ವರ್ಷ ಮದುವೆ ಆಗ್ತೀನಿ 'I'll get married next year'. Time words make the future meaning clear.

**Certainty and probability**:
• ಖಂಡಿತ + future: ಖಂಡಿತ ಮಾಡ್ತೀನಿ 'I'll definitely do it'
• -ಬಹುದು 'might': ಅವರು ತಡವಾಗಿ ಬರಬಹುದು 'they might come late'
• ಬಹುಶಃ + future: ಬಹುಶಃ ನಾಳೆ ಬರ್ತಾನೆ 'he'll probably come tomorrow'

**Future negative** is the same as the present negative: ಬರಲ್ಲ / ಬರುವುದಿಲ್ಲ 'won't come'.

**'In (time)'** = ಇನ್ನು + time + -ಅಲ್ಲಿ: ಇನ್ನು ಹತ್ತು ನಿಮಿಷದಲ್ಲಿ 'in ten minutes'. **'Before / after'** = noun/dative + ಮುಂಚೆ / ನಂತರ: ಊಟಕ್ಕೆ ಮುಂಚೆ 'before lunch', ಊಟದ ನಂತರ 'after lunch'. After a verb: ಊಟ ಮಾಡಿದ ಮೇಲೆ / ಮಾಡಿದ ನಂತರ 'after eating', ಹೋಗೋ ಮುಂಚೆ 'before going'.

examples.native: ಮುಂದಿನ ವರ್ಷ ನಾವು ಹೊಸ ಮನೆಗೆ ಹೋಗ್ತೀವಿ
examples.roman: mundina varṣa nāvu hosa manege hōgtīvi
examples.en: Next year we'll move to a new house.
It'll probably rain in the evening.
After work's done, let's go to a film.
I'm not going to that party.

grammar.title: 'Want to', 'planning to', 'I'd love to'
grammar.body:
**Want to** = **dative** subject + infinitive + **ಬೇಕು**:
• ನನಗೆ ಮನೆಗೆ ಹೋಗಬೇಕು 'I want to go home'
Compare with the **nominative** subject, which means obligation:
• ನಾನು ಮನೆಗೆ ಹೋಗಬೇಕು 'I have to go home'
(In fast speech the pronoun is often dropped and context decides.) 'Don't want to' = infinitive + ಬೇಡ, or ಮನಸ್ಸಿಲ್ಲ 'I don't feel like it'.

**Planning / thinking of** = clause + **ಅಂತ ಇದ್ದೀನಿ** 'I am (with the thought) that ...':
• ಹೋಗಬೇಕು ಅಂತ ಇದ್ದೀನಿ / ಹೋಗೋಣ ಅಂತ ಇದ್ದೀನಿ 'I'm planning to go'
• ಮಾಡಬೇಕು ಅಂತ ನಿರ್ಧರಿಸಿದ್ದೀನಿ 'I've decided to do it'

**Wish / would love to** = relative participle (-ಉವ, spoken -ಓ) + **ಆಸೆ ಇದೆ**: ನನಗೆ ಹಿಮಾಲಯ ನೋಡೋ ಆಸೆ ಇದೆ 'I'd love to see the Himalayas'.

**Fixed plans** often use the verbal noun -ಓದು: ನಾವು ಹೋಗೋದು ಶುಕ್ರವಾರ 'we're going on Friday (that's when our going is)'.

examples.en: I want to learn Kannada well.
She wants to become a doctor.

examples.native: ಮುಂದಿನ ವರ್ಷ ಕೆಲಸ ಬದಲಾಯಿಸಬೇಕು ಅಂತ ಇದ್ದೀನಿ
examples.roman: mundina varṣa kelasa badalāyisabēku anta iddīni
examples.en: I'm planning to change jobs next year.

examples.native: ನಮಗೆ ಸ್ವಂತ ಮನೆ ಕಟ್ಟೋ ಆಸೆ ಇದೆ
examples.roman: namage svanta mane kaṭṭō āse ide
examples.en: We'd love to build our own house.
We're setting off at six in the morning.

dialogue.title: Holiday plans
dialogue.setting: Colleagues Vinay and Hannah talk about their plans for the Dasara holidays.

lines.speaker: Vinay
lines.en: What's your plan for the Dasara holidays?

lines.speaker: Hannah
lines.native: ಮೈಸೂರು ದಸರಾ ನೋಡಬೇಕು ಅಂತ ಇದ್ದೀನಿ. ನೀವು?
lines.roman: maisūru dasarā nōḍabēku anta iddīni. nīvu?
lines.en: I'm planning to see the Mysuru Dasara. And you?

lines.speaker: Vinay
lines.native: ನಾನು ಊರಿಗೆ ಹೋಗ್ತೀನಿ. ಅಮ್ಮ ಹಬ್ಬಕ್ಕೆ ಬಾ ಅಂತ ಹೇಳಿದ್ದಾರೆ.
lines.roman: nānu ūrige hōgtīni. amma habbakke bā anta hēḷiddāre.
lines.en: I'm going to my hometown. Mum has told me to come for the festival.

lines.speaker: Hannah
lines.en: Your hometown is near Mysuru, isn't it?

lines.speaker: Vinay
lines.native: ಹೌದು, ಮಂಡ್ಯ. ನೀವು ಮೈಸೂರಿಗೆ ಯಾವತ್ತು ಹೋಗ್ತೀರ?
lines.roman: haudu, maṇḍya. nīvu maisūrige yāvattu hōgtīra?
lines.en: Yes, Mandya. When are you going to Mysuru?

lines.speaker: Hannah
lines.native: ವಿಜಯದಶಮಿ ದಿನ. ನನಗೆ ಜಂಬೂ ಸವಾರಿ ನೋಡೋ ಆಸೆ ಇದೆ.
lines.roman: vijayadashami dina. nanage jambū savāri nōḍō āse ide.
lines.en: On Vijayadashami day. I'd love to see the elephant procession.

lines.speaker: Vinay
lines.en: There'll be huge crowds. You'll have to go early.

lines.speaker: Hannah
lines.en: Okay. Can I come to your house afterwards?

lines.speaker: Vinay
lines.native: ಖಂಡಿತ ಬನ್ನಿ! ಅಮ್ಮ ಒಳ್ಳೆ ಹಬ್ಬದ ಊಟ ಮಾಡ್ತಾರೆ.
lines.roman: khaṇḍita banni! amma oḷḷe habbada ūṭa māḍtāre.
lines.en: Definitely, come! Mum will cook a great festival meal.

culture: **Mysuru Dasara** (ನಾಡಹಬ್ಬ, 'the state festival') lasts ten days in Sept/Oct, with the palace lit by nearly 100,000 bulbs and the ಜಂಬೂ ಸವಾರಿ elephant procession on the last day, Vijayadashami. Other big Karnataka festivals: ಯುಗಾದಿ (New Year), ಗಣೇಶ ಚತುರ್ಥಿ, ದೀಪಾವಳಿ, and ಸಂಕ್ರಾಂತಿ in January, when people exchange ಎಳ್ಳು-ಬೆಲ್ಲ (sesame and jaggery) saying ಎಳ್ಳು ಬೆಲ್ಲ ತಿಂದು ಒಳ್ಳೆ ಮಾತಾಡಿ 'eat sesame and jaggery and speak sweetly'.
